name: Chart
description: Charts drawn by CSS with no library: columns and bars (grouped, stacked, 100%, horizontal, with lines over them), histograms, waterfalls, lines and areas (stacked, stepped), scatters and bubbles, donuts, pies, gauges, radars, heatmaps, funnels, a ranked bar list and sparklines. Bars, slices, cells and ticks take --ayy-value (0–100), dots --ayy-x/--ayy-y, lines are SVG paths from chartPath(). Series colours are the chart tokens in order, so a chart library can match them.

classes.ayy-chart: Root, usually a <figure>. A grid of the plot, the labels, the legend and the data table.
classes.ayy-chart--stacked: A column's bars sit on top of each other; each bar's --ayy-value is its share of the top of the scale.
classes.ayy-chart--values: Print every bar's data-value above it (otherwise only on hover).
classes.ayy-chart--horizontal: One row per label with the bars along the reading direction: the __labels sit beside the plot, ticks become lines down it with their labels under it. Works with --stacked. Rows are 2rem.
classes.ayy-chart--histogram: Columns touch (1px apart) and fill their bins, so they read as one distribution. Label each column with its bin's start; the labels sit at the start of their column.
classes.ayy-chart--combo: Columns with lines over them: the columns split the width with no gap, so a line from chartPath(values, { band: true }) passes over their centres. Colour each line series with the next chart token (--ayy-chart-color on its __series).
classes.ayy-chart--waterfall: Floating bars, solid and rounded at both ends: each __bar starts at --ayy-start (the running total before it, 0–100) and is --ayy-value tall. Use with --values so the signed changes show.
classes.ayy-chart--pie: A solid pie: the __slice circles take r="25" and are stroked to the centre. No __total.
classes.ayy-chart--gauge: A half ring over the top (viewBox="0 0 100 50"), filled from the start side: a __track behind one __slice (or a few), with a __total under the arc. Put role="meter" and its aria-value* on the __plot.
classes.ayy-chart--radar: A square plot of an __svg with __grid rings and spokes, a __series per shape (closed __area and __line paths from chartRadar()) and an __label per spoke.
classes.ayy-chart__plot: The drawing area (aria-hidden="true"). Height from --ayy-chart-height (default 12rem); square for a donut, pie or radar, half as tall for a gauge. Holds ticks and __bars, an __svg, __series of __dots or a __ring.
classes.ayy-chart__tick: A value line across the plot, its text the label in the gutter. --ayy-value places it: 0 is the floor, 100 the top. The gutter only appears when there are ticks.
classes.ayy-chart__bars: Row of columns filling the plot.
classes.ayy-chart__column: One label's bars, side by side (or stacked).
classes.ayy-chart__bar: A bar, fading toward its base (solid when stacked): --ayy-value is its height, data-value its text on hover, --ayy-start lifts it off the floor (a floating bar). Its colour is chart-1, chart-2… by position in the column; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__bar--up: A waterfall's rise: the success colour.
classes.ayy-chart__bar--down: A waterfall's drop: the destructive colour.
classes.ayy-chart__svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> stretched over the plot, for lines and areas. Mirrors in RTL.
classes.ayy-chart__series: One series: a <g> around its area and line in an __svg, or a <div> of its __dots in a scatter. Coloured chart-1, chart-2… in order; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__series--compare: A comparison series (last period, a target): dashed, quiet, no fill.
classes.ayy-chart__line: <path> of the line, 2px whatever the stretch (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke).
classes.ayy-chart__area: <path> of the area under the line: a 16% tint of the series colour, or fill="url(#…)" an __gradient in its series to fade out toward the floor (React does).
classes.ayy-chart__gradient: A <linearGradient x2="0" y2="1"> with two <stop>s, inside the series' <g> (in <defs>): its stops take the series colour, 32% at the top to none at the floor.
classes.ayy-chart__labels: The labels under the plot (aria-hidden="true"), one per column (beside it when horizontal); under a line or a scatter they spread from the first value to the last.
classes.ayy-chart__axis: An axis name (aria-hidden="true"): before the plot it names the vertical axis, after the __labels the horizontal one, at the end.
classes.ayy-chart__dot: A scatter point (a <span> in a <div class="ayy-chart__series">): --ayy-x and --ayy-y (0–100) place it, --ayy-z (0–100) makes it a bubble up to 3rem across, data-value is its text on hover.
classes.ayy-chart__ring: <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100"> of a donut or pie ("0 0 100 50" for a gauge), filling the __plot. Turned so slices start at the top and run clockwise.
classes.ayy-chart__track: <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" pathLength="100"> behind a gauge's slices: the empty part, a faint wash.
classes.ayy-chart__slice: <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" pathLength="100"> (r="25" in a pie): a dash --ayy-value long that starts --ayy-start along the ring (chartSlices() gives both), with a hairline gap after it. Coloured chart-1, chart-2… in order; --ayy-chart-color overrides.
classes.ayy-chart__total: The number in the middle of a donut, or under a gauge's arc: an __total-value and a caption after it.
classes.ayy-chart__total-value: The total itself, in the text colour and xl.
classes.ayy-chart__grid: <path> of a radar's rings and spokes, a hairline.
classes.ayy-chart__label: A label in the plot at --ayy-x / --ayy-y, set outward from the centre (a radar's spoke names).
classes.ayy-chart__legend: List of the series, when there's more than one (aria-hidden="true" when a data table names them).
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item: A series name with its swatch, coloured in the same order as the series.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item--compare: Legend entry for a comparison series: a dashed swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-item--line: Legend entry for a line over columns (a combo): a short solid line for a swatch.
classes.ayy-chart__swatch: The colour square in a legend item.
classes.ayy-chart__legend-value: A number at the end of a legend item (a slice's share), tabular digits.
classes.ayy-bar-list: <ol> of ranked rows (top pages, sources) with the bar behind the text. Readable as it is.
classes.ayy-bar-list__item: A row; --ayy-value is the bar's length (100 = the largest). The bar fades along the row.
classes.ayy-bar-list__label: The row's name (or a link), cut with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-sparkline: A small <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"> line with no axes, for a stat or a table cell. Uses __line and __area paths.
classes.ayy-heatmap: A grid of cells (aria-hidden="true", in a figure.ayy-chart with a data table): --ayy-columns says how many columns. Its __rows hold a row label and the cells; a last row of an empty span and __labels names the columns.
classes.ayy-heatmap__row: A row: its first child is the row's __label, the rest are __cells (or column __labels). Lays its children on the heatmap's columns.
classes.ayy-heatmap__label: A row's name (first in its row, at the end of its column) or a column's name, centred under it and free to spill into empty neighbours: name every other column when they're narrow.
classes.ayy-heatmap__cell: A cell taking --ayy-value % of the series colour over a faint wash; data-value is its text on hover. --ayy-chart-color changes the colour.
classes.ayy-heatmap__key: "Less □□□□□ More" under the heatmap: two words around a few __cells (--ayy-value 0, 25, 50, 75, 100). aria-hidden="true".
classes.ayy-funnel: <ol> of the steps people drop out of, readable as it is: label, a centred bar, the value and the rate.
classes.ayy-funnel__step: A step; --ayy-value is its bar's width (100 = the first, largest step).
classes.ayy-funnel__label: The step's name, cut with an ellipsis.
classes.ayy-funnel__bar: An empty <span>: the bar, centred, in the series colour.
classes.ayy-funnel__rate: Its share of the step before (or of the first), muted. Add what it's a share of in an .ayy-sr-only span.

default.looks: Bars, lines, areas, dots, slices or cells in --ayy-chart-1… in order, muted s labels, hairline ticks; the drawing is aria-hidden and the numbers live in a table.

hover.looks: A column's bars and a slice mix 20% toward the text colour; bars show their data-value above them; a dot fills solid and a cell takes a text-colour outline, each with its data-value on a raised surface above it.

focus.none: Not focusable; the data table (or the funnel's own text, or the gauge's meter) carries the numbers.

error.none: No error look; show an Alert in its place.

loading.none: Use a block Skeleton of the chart's height while data loads; bars, slices and funnel steps grow from 0 when they appear.

sizes.density: The plot is --ayy-chart-height (12rem) tall; a donut or pie is that wide and square, a gauge that wide and half as tall, a radar 16rem square; horizontal rows are 2rem; bar-list rows and funnel bars are the sm control height; a sparkline is 6rem × 1.75rem. Chart labels and legend text follow data-density via --ayy-text-s.
sizes.width: Fills its container; columns share the width (bars at most 2.5rem wide, histogram bins all of it). A donut's legend sits beside it and wraps under it in a narrow box; a radar leaves 5rem each side for its spoke names.

js: chartScale(values, { ticks?, min?, max? }) → { min, max, ticks } with a round top; chartPercent(value, max, min?) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; chartPath(values, { min?, max?, smooth?, step?, band?, base? }) → { line, area } path data for the 0 0 100 100 box (step: steps; band: points over column centres; base: the area's floor, for stacking); chartStack(series, { percent? }) → each series' running top; chartBins(values, { bins?, min?, max? }) → { edges, counts } for a histogram; chartSlices(values, { total? }) → [{ start, value }] shares for ring slices; chartRadar(values, { min?, max? }) → a closed path and chartRadarPoint(index, count, share?, radius?) → { x, y } for spokes and labels; chartWaterfall(steps) → [{ from, to, change }]; chartColors(target?, count?) → resolved rgb() strings and chartTheme(target?) → { colors, text, muted, grid, surface, fontFamily } for canvas libraries (Chart.js, ECharts); chartClass({ stacked?, values?, horizontal?, type?, className? }) with type one of chartTypes (histogram, combo, waterfall, pie, gauge, radar), chartSeriesClass({ compare?, className? }), chartLegendItemClass({ compare?, line?, className? }) and part class constants.

react.import: import { BarChart, LineChart, HistogramChart, WaterfallChart, ScatterChart, DonutChart, GaugeChart, RadarChart, HeatmapChart, FunnelChart, Sparkline, BarList, TableChart } from "@danitesler/ayywi/react";

BarChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with a plot of __column/__bar, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — what it shows ("Signups per day"); the data table's caption
props.stacked: boolean | "percent" — percent makes every column 100% (ticks read 0%–100%)
props.showValues: boolean — print values above the bars
props.horizontal: boolean — one row per label, bars along the reading direction
props.lines: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — lines over the columns on the same scale (a combo); not with horizontal
props.max: number — top of the scale; rounded up from the data if omitted
props.ticks: number of value lines, default 3; 0 for none
props.format: (value: number) => string — ticks, hover values and the table; default compact (1.2K)
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series

LineChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with an __svg of __series paths, labels, a legend and a visually hidden data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.series: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — compare draws a dashed comparison line
props.smooth: boolean, default true (monotone: never overshoots a point)
props.step: boolean — steps, each value held until halfway to the next
props.stacked: boolean — each area on the series before it, the top line the total; compare series stay apart

HistogramChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--histogram"> of touching columns, one per bin, each bin's start under it, and a data table of bin ranges

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.values: number[] — the raw values, counted into bins
props.bins: number — about how many; edges are rounded. Default about √n, at most 20
props.range: [min, max] — the values the bins cover; default the data's
props.name: string — what's counted, the table's column header; default label
props.max: number — top of the count scale

WaterfallChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--values ayy-chart--waterfall"> of floating bars, signed values above them, and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.steps: { label, value, total? }[] — changes (negative for a drop) and totals (from zero)
props.name: string — the table's column header; default label
props.min: number — default 0, or the lowest running total below it
props.format: (value: number) => string — the sign is added for changes

ScatterChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with axis names, a plot of __series of __dots, x labels, a legend and a data table of the points

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.series: { name, points: { x, y, z?, label? }[], color? }[] — z sizes bubbles (by area)
props.zLabel: string — the bubble size's name in the table
props.xMin / xMax / yMin / yMax: number — the scales' ends; the minimums default to 0, the tops are rounded up
props.ticks: number of values along each axis, default 3; 0 for none
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series

DonutChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with a __ring of __slices, the __total in the middle, a legend of shares beside it and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.items: { name, value, color? }[] — the parts; six at most
props.pie: boolean — a solid pie, no total
props.total: ReactNode — the number in the middle; default the formatted sum
props.name: string — the table's column header; default label
props.size: CSS length — the ring's width, default 12rem

GaugeChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--gauge"> with a role="meter" plot: a half __ring, its __track and a __slice, the value under it

props.label: string — the meter's name ("Ad spend this month")
props.totalLabel: string — under the value and in aria-valuetext ("of $10K")
props.color: CSS colour, default chart-1 (warning past a limit)
props.size: CSS length — the arc's width, default 12rem

RadarChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart ayy-chart--radar"> with a square __svg of rings, spokes and __series shapes, spoke __labels, a legend and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.axes: string[] — one per spoke, clockwise from the top
props.series: { name, values: number[], color?, compare? }[] — compare: dashed, no fill
props.max: number — the outer ring; rounded up from the data
props.ticks: number of rings counting the centre, default 5
props.size: CSS length — the plot's width, default 16rem
props.legend: boolean — default: more than one series

HeatmapChart.renders: <figure class="ayy-chart"> with an .ayy-heatmap of rows, a Less–More key and a data table

props.label: string — the data table's caption
props.columns: string[] — column names, every other one shown past eight
props.max: number — the darkest cell; default the largest value
props.legend: [less, more] | false — the key's words, default ["Less", "More"]

FunnelChart.renders: <ol class="ayy-funnel"> of steps with centred bars, values and rates

props.rate: "previous" | "first" — what each rate is a share of, default previous
props.rateLabel: string — read after each rate by screen readers; default "of the step before" / "of the first step"

props.label: string — makes it role="img" with this name; without it the sparkline is aria-hidden

props.max: number — value of a full bar, default the largest

TableChart.renders: <div class="ayy-table-wrap"><table class="ayy-table"> with headers, swatches and numeric cells

props.label: string — what it shows; the table's caption
props.labels: string[] — one per row along the side
props.format: (value: number) => string — cell values; default compact (1.2K)

a11y: The drawing is aria-hidden. The numbers go in a table with a <caption> saying what the chart shows, inside a <div class="ayy-sr-only"> (as React renders it): a table can't be narrower than its content, so hiding the table itself lets a long caption widen the page. Add a visible Table if people need to compare values.
Don't rely on colour alone: a legend names the series in the same order, the comparison series is dashed, and a title or a Stat states the takeaway ("Up 12% on last week").
Series tokens keep 3:1 against every surface in every theme. In High Contrast bars and lines take system colours, alternating between CanvasText and Highlight.
A Sparkline with a label is an image with that name; give it the trend in words ("Revenue, last 14 days, up 12%").

A gauge is one value, so it's a meter: role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, an aria-valuetext in words ("$7.2K of $10K") and a name. A funnel and a bar list are text already and need no table.
Waterfall changes are signed (+$6.4K, −$1.3K) as well as coloured, and a donut's legend gives each share as a number.
do: Use a chart to show a trend or a comparison at a glance: signups per day, revenue against last month, traffic by source. Put it in a Card with the title and the key number (a Stat) above it.

Pick the form from the question: columns to compare amounts across periods (horizontal bars when the labels are long), stacked or 100% columns for parts over time, a line for a trend over many points (stacked areas for a total and its parts, steps for values that jump), a combo for amounts with their average or target, a histogram for how values spread, a waterfall for how one total became another, a scatter for how two measures relate (bubbles for a third), a donut or pie for a few parts of one whole, a gauge for one value against its limit, a radar to compare a few profiles over five to eight measures, a heatmap for activity by two dimensions (day × hour), a funnel for the steps people drop out of, a bar list for a ranking, a sparkline beside a number.
Colour series with the chart tokens in order (React does it). With a chart library, pass var(--ayy-chart-1)… (SVG) or chartColors() (canvas), and chartTheme() for its text, grid and tooltip.
Mark the previous period as a compare series instead of a second bright colour.
Keep the scale honest: bars start at 0; let chartScale() round the top.
dont: Don't use a chart when the exact numbers matter more than the shape — use a Table.
Don't use a donut or pie for more than five or six parts, for parts that are close in size, or to compare wholes — a Bar list or stacked columns are easier to read.
Don't use a radar for more than three series or for measures on different scales — use columns or a Table.
Don't use a gauge for a value with no meaningful maximum — use a Stat with a Sparkline.
Don't pick series colours from the status or accent tokens unless the colour means something (success for a goal line).
Don't draw more than six series; group the rest as Other.
Don't add a second chart library just for a simple bar or line — these cover dashboards. Reach for one (Recharts, Chart.js) for zoom, brushing or maps, themed with the tokens.
